📉 Crossings are down. The bill is still enormous. That tells you everything.

I'll be straight with you, because that's how you keep your credibility: the numbers HAVE fallen. Around 16,400 Channel crossings between January and 1 September — about 43% down on last year. Asylum claims down 21%. The backlog down 56%.

Good. Now the question nobody in Whitehall wants asked 👇

💷 Asylum accommodation contracts originally estimated at £4.5bn are now forecast at around £15.3bn over ten years.
🏨 In 2024/25 hotels swallowed 76% of the annual contract cost — while housing just 35% of the people.

Falling numbers plus a rising bill means the cost isn't being driven by volume. It's being driven by the system. This is a procurement failure as much as an immigration one — and you're paying for it.
